channel.title: LLM Vibes Research
channel.description: Independent analysis of AI model quality and incidents from the LLM Vibes data set.

item.title: The first Astra opened at 69% positive. GPT-6.2 opened at 43%.
item.description: OpenAI called GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol a new standard for professional work. One early reviewer called them unusable, and Sam Altman's own launch thread said they need to be nicer to work with. In two samples, about 4 in 10 posts that took a side were positive. For the first Astra it was 7 in 10.

item.title: Opus 5.5 got the warmest Claude launch we've measured. Opus 5 looked warm too, for three days.
item.description: Everyone was waiting for an Opus 5.1 to fix Opus 5. Anthropic shipped Opus 5.5 instead, and over six days the Claude score rose 27 points and posts naming it warmed up after day two. Opus 5 opened strong too, then cooled by day four. OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol and Luna launched the same day and landed flat.

item.title: Fable 5's launch took 17% of tracked AI chatter. Its return from the government ban took 23%.
item.description: Launched June 9, suspended by government directive June 12, redeployed behind a stricter classifier July 1, then kept in paid plans after two deadline extensions. Its return week drew 23% of tracked AI chatter, against 17% for launch week.

item.title: Grok 4.5's launch pop faded in five days. Nine days in, its share of chatter was still triple.
item.description: What holds up from a messy measurement week: a tripled share of voice that was still there nine days in, a five-day sentiment pop, a feed that flipped from Musk posts to product posts, and a switching story that's real but smaller and more price-driven than the headlines.

item.title: Claude Code lost 19 points during the cache bug. The rest of Claude lost 4.
item.description: Aggregate model scores treat each frontier model as one product. Sliced by product surface across two months of public posts, Claude Code's score fell about 19 points during the cache-bug window while the rest of Claude fell about 4, and most of that gap opened in the last five days.

item.title: We caught Claude's March slide 28 days before Anthropic confirmed it
item.description: Independent sentiment data caught Claude grumbling on March 26, the day Anthropic shipped the cache bug. 28 days before the postmortem.

item.title: How LLM Vibes classifies sentiment
item.description: How the pipeline goes from scraped post to daily score: five sources, one LLM grader, a fixed-mix 0–100 score that holds each source at its usual share, and the limitations I know about.

item.title: On average, Claude outscored ChatGPT during its own regression. The change gave it away.
item.description: During the March 2026 cache bug, Claude averaged 48 and ChatGPT 32, so a side-by-side read said Claude was fine. Against each model's own six days before, Claude fell 11 points while ChatGPT rose 6. Compare a model with its own recent past, not with its neighbors.
